verdict.rationale: Lium documents several real-time availability surfaces you can check before renting, all without an account. These are a public JSON feed of every rentable node, a public WebSocket that pushes which executors are rentable now, and MCP tools (`search_gpus`, `get_gpu_prices`) for live GPU prices and availability. GPU-type filtering is implied by GPU search, but nothing in the evidence shows availability broken down by region. missing for 10: region-level availability breakdown, explicit documentation of per-GPU-type availability fields, independent or hands-on corroboration that the feeds reflect live stock.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can see real-time GPU availability by type and region before I try to provision, instead of discovering stockouts by failure

citations.quote: Every rentable GPU node on Lium in one JSON call. No key, no signup.
A public WebSocket that keeps you up to date on which executors are rentable now. Use it instead of polling `GET /executors`. No API key needed.
